title: Workload API socket is created world-accessible and chmod 0600 only after bind
description:
HYGIENE / narrow race. Not exploitable under a normal umask.

persona-grpc/src/server.rs:23-33:
    if let Some(parent) = socket_path.parent() { std::fs::create_dir_all(parent)?; }
    let listener = UnixListener::bind(socket_path)?;
    std::fs::set_permissions(socket_path, Permissions::from_mode(0o600))?;

Two ordering problems:
1. The socket exists with mode 0777 & ~umask from bind() until set_permissions() runs. Under the usual umask 022 that is 0755 - no write bit for others, and connect(2) on a Unix socket requires write, so nobody else can connect. Under umask 000 (a daemon started from a supervisor that clears its umask, or any parent that set it) the window is 0777 and any local user can connect and be served during it.
2. create_dir_all() creates /run/user/{uid}/persona (personad/src/main.rs:53) with 0777 & ~umask and it is never tightened. Directory permissions persist after the process exits.

CONSEQUENCE during the window: a connecting process reaches fetch_jwtsvid, which does not identify its peer at all (see persona-5s4b.46 - attest_peer is never called), so it receives a JWT-SVID for the users identity. The window is microseconds and requires an unusual umask, hence P2 rather than P0.

Note this is the only thing enforcing the same-uid boundary in practice: the uid check in consumer_attest.rs:20-26 is in dead code. That makes the socket mode load-bearing and worth making unconditional.

Fix direction: the constraint, not the mechanism - set umask to 0077 around bind (or bind inside a directory created 0700 with fs::set_permissions before bind), so the socket is never briefly permissive rather than being fixed up afterwards.
close_reason: PARTLY STALE; residual fixed in 56efa94. The bead's two ordering problems: (1) the create_dir_all-under-umask half was already fixed -- server.rs prepare_socket_dir creates the directory 0700, tightens an owned directory that is too permissive, and refuses a directory another user owns. (2) The socket-mode window is real but unreachable, and the bead's own fix direction (umask around bind) was rejected: umask is per-process state shared by every thread, so setting and restoring it in an async daemon changes the mode of files other tokio workers create concurrently. The actual enforcement is the 0700 parent -- connect(2) needs search permission on it, and it exists before the socket does -- which is now recorded in the bind_listener doc comment. What WAS wrong and is now fixed: remove_file ran BEFORE prepare_socket_dir, so on the path where the daemon refuses a directory another user owns it had already unlinked a file inside it. Binding now prepares the directory first. Also fixed alongside: the stale-socket unlink was behind an exists() test, which follows symlinks and so reported false for a dangling symlink at the socket path; bind(2) then failed EADDRINUSE and the operator was told personad was already running. Three tests added, all mutation-verified (socket 0600, dir 0700, dangling symlink, and directory-vetted-before-unlink). The ordering test was VACUOUS on first writing -- it used /usr, where remove_file returns NotFound either way -- and was rewritten to use a parent that is a regular file, where the two orders give distinguishable errors.
